minutes.headline: Commission favored Marshall Park design option two, passed three FY23 funding requests to the town manager, and set conditions for the skatepark.
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission reviewed two preliminary Marshall Park concept designs from the landscape architects and civil engineer, took commissioner and public feedback, and leaned toward option two. It then voted to send funding requests for FY23 to the state delegation via the town manager, and discussed what conditions to place on the privately funded skatepark. Earlier minutes were approved except January 6, and the group agreed to gather more public feedback by survey.

public_comment.topic: Skatepark relocation details to be coordinated with engineers; agreed parking on Chestnut Street would not fix the parking problem.
Objected to shared outfield between softball and baseball, loss of T-ball field, and loss of a field under option one; asked about batting cages and snack shack.
Concern about softball seasons lost during construction, timeline, restroom and snack shack operation and maintenance responsibility.
Offered coordination on septic design and skatepark; as abutter at 105 Chestnut Street urged coordinated parking and foul ball consideration.
Concern about losing a softball or T-ball field, summer league overlap, and parking near Fitzgerald on Reservoir Road.
Liked aesthetics of plan one but supports a combined approach; favored basketball court, asked about septic versus sewer and sidewalks, and Chestnut Street parking restrictions.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager asked for projects needing funding in FY23 with dollar figures. The Marshall Park survey is in capital planning and could be funded through the state instead.
A member said the survey figure is a good number to get a survey done for Marshall Park.
A prefabricated restroom building was estimated at a range from a manufacturer quote; the septic funding from the Board of Health is already in place.

budget_items.topic: Northfield park master plan and survey
budget_items.what_was_said: Members estimated a master plan and survey for the Northfield property, comparing to the Marshall Park master plan request.
The Board of Health has money available for rehabilitating the septic system, so septic is kept as an option alongside sewer.
The skatepark group said it is investing a large sum privately in infrastructure as a gift to the town with no public dollars.
A member asked that all items also be submitted for ARPA funding; the town hired a consultant to present on February 1.
Discussion of when to issue the RFP for the civil survey relative to funding available after July 1.

decisions.decision: Commission preference for design option two; the consultants will likely develop two options built on option two.
Chair will also pass Fitzgerald field improvements to the town manager and speak with the Conservation Commission chair.
Chair will talk to the procurement contact about starting the Marshall Park survey RFP, probably around March or April.
Commissioners to email questions for the skatepark; chair will compile a list and send to town counsel and town manager.
A simple survey modeled on the town's will gather public feedback on the designs, closing February 6, with results to the consultants on February 7.
Next regular meeting set for February 17.
Portable toilets for the 2023 season will be an agenda item next meeting; the open commission seat is posted with applications through January 29.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission leaned toward Marshall Park design option two, and the consultants will likely develop two options built on it.
By roll call, all four voting aye, the commission sent three FY23 funding requests to the town manager for the legislative delegation.
The requests are Marshall Park restroom improvements, a Northfield master plan and survey, and a Marshall Park survey.
A motion not to discuss the two designs publicly that evening was withdrawn after a dispute, and the designs were presented and taken to public comment.
Commissioners will email skatepark questions to the chair, who will send a compiled list to town counsel and the town manager.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park's layout, including the fate of ball fields and parking raised by neighbors and leagues, is being shaped now, before any construction money is voted.
The three requests seek state funding through the legislative delegation, which could put the work on a different funding route than the town's own capital budget.
watch_next: A public survey on the park designs closes February 6, with results due to the consultants on February 7.
The next regular meeting is February 17, with portable toilets for the 2023 season on the agenda.
